extracted.intended_audience: mathematical researchers, MFO participants, institute stakeholders, funders and the interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Annual institutional report describing the Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach's 2015 programs, surveys, exhibitions (MiMa, IMAGINARY), administration, finances and policies. Contains program evaluation metrics and operational standards used by the institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visitor survey methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2015 the MFO sent an electronic questionnaire to all participants of the scientific programs since 2009. The questionnaire contained items concerning overall satisfaction, perceived scientific benefits, as well as service and facilities. The items had to be rated on a 10 point Likert scale, with 10 points being excellent and 1 point being poor. Furthermore, the questionnaire included several open items to complement, explain or comment on the quantitative ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large sample: more than 3,200 answered questionnaires (~from ~10,000 visitors over 7 years). Use both closed (10-point Likert) and open responses to inform policy changes and improvements (examples below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item labelled 'Overall satisfaction' measured on the 10-point Likert scale (1 poor – 10 excellent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported to be 'very high' in 2015 survey results; used as a high-level indicator of perceived quality of research stays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item labelled 'Scientific benefits' (rated on 10-point Likert scale) assessing perceived scientific usefulness of a stay at MFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated 'nearly excellent'; complemented by over 1,000 responses listing publications that arose from stays and >1,000 descriptions of positive career impact (examples of testimonial outcomes given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item 'Service and facilities' rated on the 10-point Likert scale to evaluate institutional services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside more specific facility items to identify improvement areas (e.g., internet policy change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the scientific program (talks and lectures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey dimension explicitly named 'Quality of the scientific program (talks and lectures)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates scientific content delivered at events; contributes to 'overall satisfaction' and to perceived scientific benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific contacts and discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item 'Scientific contacts and discussions' measuring opportunity for networking, informal and formal discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimonials emphasise networking value (collaborations, job references, initiation of papers); considered a core success metric for workshops and programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulation/initiation of new research projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey dimension 'Stimulation/initiation of new research projects' (10-point scale) to assess whether stays initiate new lines of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High ratings and testimonial examples indicate research projects and publications initiated at Oberwolfach; used as evidence of scientific impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research facilities (lecture/discussion rooms, equipment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item 'Research facilities, (lecture/discussion rooms, equipment)' evaluating physical infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to judge adequacy of rooms and technical equipment for scientific work; informs investment decisions (e.g., new discussion rooms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Library (literature, electronic services, reading places)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item 'Library (literature, electronic services, reading places)' assessing library services and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratings and comments guide library service improvements and investments in electronic access.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT (information/communication, technical equipment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item 'IT (information/communication, technical equipment)' to evaluate IT support and infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback (e.g., complaints about internet access policy in guest rooms) led to concrete policy change (see Internet access policy entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest house (board and lodging)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item 'Guest house (board and lodging)' to evaluate accommodation and catering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratings inform housekeeping and lodging provisions (single rooms, apartments, bungalows) and catering services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support by staff prior to your stay
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item 'Support by staff prior to your stay' measuring administrative responsiveness before visits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to monitor organisation and front-line administrative effectiveness; part of service quality metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support by staff during and after your stay
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item 'Support by staff during and after your stay' measuring support quality while on-site and follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratings used to evaluate staff performance and to identify areas for process improvement in guest liaison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of survey feedback to change policies
rubrics_metrics.description: The institute uses aggregated survey feedback and open comments to decide on policy changes (example: internet access policy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: criticism of prior policy limiting internet access in guest rooms to night hours led to decision to provide internet 24/7. Other feedback informed plans to create more discussion rooms for smaller groups. Implementation requires analysis and feasibility checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mineral exhibition focus (Black Forest, Clara mine)
rubrics_metrics.description: MiMa's mineral exhibition is deliberately focused on finds from the Black Forest to comprehensively present the region's mineralogical diversity; a special emphasis is placed on minerals of the still-active 'Clara' mine in Oberwolfach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curatorial criterion: prefer regional specimens to highlight local uniqueness and tie to institute location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math exhibition design: interactive, hands-on, applied and pure math, crystallography focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The maths exhibition 'offers aesthetic insights into mathematics and enables visitors to playfully explore mathematical phenomena. Interactive programs, hands-on exhibits, and images depict concepts of both applied and pure mathematics. A clear focus is put on the mathematical foundations of crystallography.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit design standard: prioritize interactive, tactile, and visual experiences; include both applied and pure topics; ensure thematic linkage (e.g., between minerals and mathematical forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum visitor resources (audio guide, teacher school package, regional map)
rubrics_metrics.description: MiMa offers visitor services: a free audio guide downloadable prior to the visit, a school package for teachers with introduction videos and background material suggestions, and an overview map with recommended regional museums and leisure facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service criteria: provide pre-visit downloadable resources, educational packs for teachers, and regional orientation materials to enhance accessibility and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit composition standards (touchscreens, hands-on stations, image gallery, crystals display)
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful exhibitions described include components such as interactive touch-screen stations, hands-on experiment stations, film stations, mathematical image galleries and curated crystal displays in glass cabinets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curation checklist: combine digital interactivity, tactile experiments, visual galleries and physical specimens to serve diverse audiences and learning modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMAGINARY platform standards (open source, free license, community contributions, multilingual)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMAGINARY provides an open source platform for interactive math exhibits; all content is made available under a free license, users can contribute their own content, and the platform is multilingual (in 2015: versions in up to six languages; major exhibits translated into additional languages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for dissemination: use free licensing to enable reuse, support community contributions, and provide multilingual access to broaden reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition documentation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: IMAGINARY stores organized documentation for events: descriptions plus photos and for some events videos; in 2015 IMAGINARY organized 56 exhibition activities recorded in the platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation requirement: maintain an event record with media to allow reuse, evaluation, and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition collaboration & infrastructure development
rubrics_metrics.description: IMAGINARY collaborates with research and museum partners (e.g., HITS, ESO Supernova) to develop software infrastructures and dynamic museum systems, with added control and management tools for museums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative criterion: partner with institutes to develop sustainable digital infrastructure; plan for museum-specific management features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local IT infrastructure policy (own cloud server for Snapshots project)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Snapshots of Modern Mathematics from Oberwolfach' project led to setup of an owncloud server hosted at the MFO to permit efficient, location-independent collaboration while keeping data under the Institute's control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IT policy preference: host collaboration services in-house where possible to retain data control and enable flexible workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program budget requirement (GWK / Leibniz Association rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: According to resolutions of the Gemeinsame Wissenschaftskonferenz (GWK), as a member of the Leibniz Association, the MFO has prepared a program budget since 2006 as the basis for joint financing by the federation and the federal states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial governance standard: prepare and publish a program budget to meet joint-funding requirements and ensure transparency for public funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party funds accounting practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party funds were attributed to the fiscal year for which they were assigned; earmarked surpluses from previous years are reported separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounting rule: attribute external grants to the fiscal year of assignment and report earmarked carry-forwards transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting private resource proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: The report discloses the share of private resources (third-party funds, donations and other income) as a percentage of total revenues (21.5% in 2015, excluding earmarked surpluses from 2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial reporting standard: quantify and publish the fraction of non-public funding to demonstrate diversification of revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest accommodation standards (single rooms, apartments, bungalows)
rubrics_metrics.description: Board and lodging are provided by the Institute: scientists are mostly housed in single rooms; the guest house also provides 8 larger apartments and 5 bungalows enabling longer stays (e.g., Research in Pairs program, Leibniz Fellows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accommodation criterion: provide a mix of single rooms and larger units to support varying lengths and formats of stays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housekeeping and staffing levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Housekeeping comprises 13 positions for kitchen and room service and for maintenance; administrative area encompasses 13.77 FTE for scientific administration, library, IT and general administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational standard: staff levels and role descriptions should be reported and aligned with program needs (workshops, seminars, library services, guest support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisational governance representation and advisory composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Governance: the MFO is funded jointly by federation and federal states and is a member of the Leibniz Association. The Administrative Council includes representatives of funding partners and decides on medium- and long-term budget planning. The institute is advised by a Scientific Advisory Board (6 to 8 internationally renowned mathematicians). The GMF (Gesellschaft für Mathematische Forschung e.V.) holds the institute's property and the Scientific Committee (≈20–25 mathematicians) is responsible for R&D planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance criterion: ensure funder representation in supervisory bodies, maintain an international scientific advisory board, and separate legal ownership and scientific planning responsibilities for institutional stability.
